Is this a RTX 3050 review or an excuse to keep shitting on the RX 6500 XT? We get it, the 6500 XT is a product with some glaring limitations and the 3050 beats it by a fair amount. No one is surprised that a cut down GA106 based card beats a Navi 24 based card.

The 3050 has 8 gigs of VRAM, which is clearly overkill. Both the 2060 and 5600 XT have 6 gigs of VRAM and still beat the 3050 in everything except Doom Eternal at 1440p Ultra settings. What does 8GB do instead of 6GB? First of all it ups the price. Last I heard from MLID, GDDR6 was $12 per gig (discussed in a 3060 video on why that card has 12GB), so that's at least $24 that could have been saved, a bit more if every party's cut on that is also gone. A 6GB 3050 with a MSRP of $225 would have crushed the 6500 XT and anything else in that range. It does make the 3050 more viable for mining though, so we can expect stock to be at zero all the time. Miners with enough money for 2 3060 cards can buy 3 3050 cards and Nvidia are the overall winners there.

Oh and let's not forget the "essential" features like 4 display outputs instead of the measly 2 the 6500 XT has, because all gamers are running at least 3 monitors, right?

But, you know, it stomps a GPU designed for laptops that was pushed to desktop for no good reason, so let's focus on that instead. comments.text: You mentioned power efficiency at 13:34, noting that total system power usage is only 15% higher than the 6500XT. While I do like you mentioning total system power (since it's context is often forgotten), I would argue that a 15% difference is not what the average budget GPU owner will see. This percentage difference relies on all parts of the system, and a budget build total system power won't include overpowered parts from this test system such as the 5950X. I think if a total system power comparison is going to be made, then the systems being used need to be realistic. For example: with a basic 60 watt cpu, modest RAM, an SSD and/or NVME drive, I would expect total system power (without GPU) to be under 100 watts. That means with a 6500XT probably a bit under 200 watts for total system power, and now that 36 watt difference is closer to 20% of total system power, not 15%. Obviously not a huge difference, and in this case doesn't really change any conclusions, but I think this it is worth mentioning if you're going to call out percentage differences in 'total system power', when the 'total system' isn't actually a normal build and has factors skewing it such as a cpu that's a lot more power-hungry than any reasonable build with a budget GPU would have.

I would say it is impressive for a card crippled in so many ways (low RAM, 64bit RAM bus, 4 lanes of PCI-E) to be able to provide 85% of performance of the RTX 3050 when the game fits into it's own memory.
